html:
A Japanese franchise about catching, training and trading creatures called Pokémon, which began in 1996 with two games for Nintendo's Game Boy, Pokémon Red and Green.

The idea came from Satoshi Tajiri of the studio Game Freak, who had collected insects as a boy. Players had to trade with friends over a link cable to complete their collection, which made the game social. A trading card game followed in 1996 and an anime series in 1997, with Pikachu as its face.

By the end of the 1990s it was a craze across North America and Europe. Later games, films, toys and the phone game Pokémon Go of 2016 kept it going. It is often counted as the highest grossing media franchise in the world.

With manga, anime and video games, Pokémon is a core part of the soft power of modern Japan.
sum: A Japanese franchise about catching, training and trading creatures called Pokémon, which began in 1996 with two games for Nintendo's Game Boy, Pokémon Red and Green.
